page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Two heads are better than one
title: Two heads are better than one
description:
The company in France that Anna called earlier has returned her call. She hopes they're about to place an order which could help save Tip Top Trading from closure. But this deal will involve some negotiation and Anna needs some help.
This episode focuses on what to say when negotiating a deal with a client.
phrases: What kind of price are you willing to pay?
I don't think we can go that low.
If you buy more stock I can offer you a bigger discount.

listening_challenge.question:
What does the company in France agree to buy from Tip Top Trading?
5,000 Imperial Lemons.
listening_challenge.answer:
What does the company in France agree to buy from Tip Top Trading?
5,000 Imperial Lemons.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: (On the phone) Yes, we have plenty in stock. They're £4 per unit… They are good quality ones…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The company in France that Anna called earlier has called her back. Let's hope they're making an order.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …laser technology isn't cheap… hmm, I see… Well, thanks for calling back. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Everything OK Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Not really. One of the companies I cold called has rung back…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Good, good…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …but they don't want to place an order. They say we're too expensive.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So you let them go? Didn't you negotiate with them?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, was I meant to? I wasn't sure what to say.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Having trouble Anna? Don't worry, I'm sure that I can help. Negotiating is my thing!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: "Negotiating is my thing"! What is he like? Mind you, he has won a Pear Salesman of the Year award so he must be doing something right.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Are you sure Tom? Don't you want to negotiate your own deals?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I owe you one Anna after you saved my bacon with Mr Socrates the other night. And besides you and me…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Come on you two. Get a move on. Europe is waiting for us! Custard cream anyone?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No thanks. Right. Now you need to call that French company back and ask them what kind of price they are willing to pay.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And then say that's fine?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No! Negotiate. Say "I don't think we can go that low".

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: "I don't think we can go that low".

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: If they want a bigger discount, tell them they will have to buy more stock.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: More stock, bigger discount.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah. And if you still can't agree a price, tell them "I'll meet you halfway".

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Meet halfway?! That means going to Paris!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No. Halfway on the price. That line always works for me. I sold a load of plastic pears that way once.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: So that's "I'll meet you halfway". Thanks Tom. I'm really impressed. You… you…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Am I, really?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What? I was going to say, you really do know your stuff – despite what other people say.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What? Uh?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right, I'm off to make that call right now.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Good luck Anna and well done Tom! Nice to hear him give some useful advice but will it work? Let's remind ourselves of the phrases he suggested Anna uses when negotiating a sale:
What kind of price are you willing to pay?
I don't think we can go that low.
If you buy more stock, I can offer you a bigger discount.
I'll meet you halfway.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Let's see how Anna has got on.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Success! They've agreed to buy 5,000 Imperial Lemons.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Brilliant. I knew you would be great. Did those killer lines of mine work?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sort of – but when I said what price were they looking to pay, they said the full price! As long as I send them the contract today so I'd better go and get an envelope and post it as soon as I can.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh great.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom… Tom… can you come over here to the stationery cupboard and get an envelope from the top shelf for me?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, suppose so… I'm coming... (Door slams shut) …oh!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh Tom, why did you do that? It won't open… it's locked… help, help!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Help!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Uh oh. This should be interesting. How are they going to explain being locked in the stationery cupboard? Until next time. Bye!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Let us out! We're stuck!
